STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r10.claim: The accounts of Zachariah, Mary, Abraham, and Moses pair divine gifts of prophetic children or relatives with each figure’s withdrawal from their people and worldly separation.
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r10.anchor: In all four accounts these Divine “gifts” are granted only after Zachariah, Mary, Abraham, and Moses withdraw from their people and enter a state of separation from the world

BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r3.claim: Peace means God's safety and protection for John in the most frightening passages; a nominal sentence expresses its enduring stability through them.
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r3.anchor: سلامة من الله تعالى وأمان {عليه} على يحيى

BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r4.claim: At birth John is protected from Satan's sting, at death from death's terror and grave punishment, and at resurrection from the terror of Judgment and Hell.
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r4.anchor: {يوم ولد} من رحم أمه من طعن الشيطان كما يطعن سائر بني آدم {ويوم يموت}

BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r5.claim: The inward reading makes birth emergence from nature, death annihilation of nature's demands in God, and resurrection subsistence after annihilation.
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى الولادة من أم الطبيعة والموت بالفناء عن مقتضيات الطبيعة في الله والبعث بالبقاء بعد الفناء

BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r6.speaker: ابن أبي عيينة
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abi Uyayna says birth, death, and resurrection are a person's loneliest moments: each brings him into an unfamiliar state, so John was singled out for peace in them.
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r6.anchor: أوحش ما يكون الإنسان في هذه الأحوال يوم ولد فيخرج مما كان ويوم يموت

BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r7.claim: Bursevi begins an inward allegory: Zakariyya is the human spirit, his wife the bodily frame, and John the heart receptive to divine effusion after the spirit doubts such a heart can arise from long bodily attachment.
BURSEVI:v5p245#3/r7.anchor: زكريا إشارة إلى الروح الإنساني وامرأته إلى الجثة الجسدانية التي هي زوج الروح ويحيى إلى القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r1.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r1.claim: Al-Tabari interprets salām as God's protection: from Satan at birth, loneliness and grave punishment at death, and judgment's terror and fire at resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r1.anchor: قال الطبري : أمان من الله تعالى عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r2.claim: The death wording supports calling a murdered person dead, in light of the report that John was killed by an Israelite prostitute.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r2.anchor: وفيه دليل على أنه يقال للمقتول ميت بناء على أنه عليه السلام قتل لبغي من بغايا بني إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r3.claim: The final ḥayyan may emphasize resurrection, establish bodily rather than spiritual resurrection, or identify John as a martyr.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r3.anchor: وجيء بالحال للتأكيد وقيل : للإشارة إلى أن البعث جسماني لا روحاني وقيل للتنبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers the ordinary greeting and honor from God at life's moments of greatest vulnerability and need.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r4.anchor: الأظهر أن المراد بالسلام التحية المتعارفة والتشريف بها لكونها من الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r5.claim: A report says Jesus and John met as maternal cousins: each asked the other to pray, and Jesus noted that God had greeted John while he had only greeted himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r5.anchor: وجاء في خبر رواه أحمد في الزهد وغيره عن الحسن أن عيسى ويحيى عليهما السلام التقيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r6.claim: The sentence semantically continues John's gifts; its nominal form expresses permanence and closes the preceding account.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p73#3/r6.anchor: عدل إلى الجملة الإسمية لإرادة الدوام والثبوت وهي كالخاتمة للكلام السابق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222#2/r3.claim: Salām means safety for Yaḥyā at birth, death, and resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222#2/r3.anchor: {وسلام عليه} أي: سلامة له، {يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222#2/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222#2/r4.claim: The three states are especially lonely: birth leaves one's former place, death brings unfamiliar people, and resurrection brings an unseen gathering; Yaḥyā is granted safety at them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p222#2/r4.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة: أوحش 6/ب (2) ما يكون الإنسان في هذه الأحوال: يوم ولد فيخرج مما كان فيه،

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r3.claim: God's peace protects Yahya at birth from Satan's harm to humans, at death from the grave's punishment, and at resurrection from the Fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:13-15/r3.anchor: من أن يناله الشيطان بما ينال به بني آدم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r2.claim: Peace protects Yahya from religious harm at birth, the distress of death and what follows, and every fear after resurrection; the three moments are the hardest, so safety then entails safety elsewhere.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r2.anchor: من كل سوء يلحق بالولادة وما بعدها في شيء من أمر الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r3.claim: The author suggests the greeting is indefinite because Yahya was killed and his body was not preserved in peace, unlike Jesus in the following passage.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r3.anchor: ولعله نكر السلام لأنه قتل فما سلم بدنه بخلاف ما يأتي في عيسى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says every child of Adam meets God with a sin and may be punished or forgiven, except Yahya, described as noble, chaste, prophetic, and righteous; the Prophet indicates that his remembrance is tiny as a speck.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r4.anchor: كل بني آدم يلقى الله يوم القيامة بذنب وقد يعذبه عليه إن شاء أو يرحمه إلا يحيى بن زكريا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r5.speaker: الهيثمي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r5.claim: Al-Haythami grades the Abu Hurayra report as having Hajjaj b. Sulayman, whom Ibn Hibban and others trusted while Abu Zurʿa and others weakened; the remaining narrators are trustworthy.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r5.anchor: وفيه حجاج ابن سليمان الرعيني وثقه ابن حبان وغيره وضعفه أبو زرعة وغيره

BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r8.claim: The stages of human development refute claims that God has a child: both child and parent depend on need, incompatible with divine independence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p525/r8.anchor: من حيث إن ذلك قاض على الولد نفسه وعلى أبيه بالحاجة

DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r1.claim: The verse's peace is God's greeting to Yahya at birth, death, and resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r1.anchor: {وسلام عليه} يعني حين سلم الله عليه {يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا}

DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r2.speaker: مالك
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r2.claim: Malik reports Jesus and Yahya were maternal cousins, conceived together; Yahya's mother saw her fetus bow to Mary's.
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r2.anchor: قال مالك: بلغني أن عيسى ابن مريم ويحيى بن زكريا عليهما السلام ابنا خالة وكان حملهما جميعا معا

DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r3.speaker: مالك
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r3.claim: Malik takes the prostration as honoring Jesus, who raised the dead and healed; Yahya ate plants and wept from fear of God until tears wore a track in his face.
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r3.anchor: قال مالك: أرى ذلك لتفضيل الله عيسى لأن الله جعله يحيي الموتى ويبرئ الأكمه والأبرص

DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r6.claim: The Prophet names Yahya as martyr son of martyr, wearing wool and eating plants from fear of sin.
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r6.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: وأين الشهيد ابن الشهيد يلبس الوبر ويأكل الشجر مخافة الذنب

DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r7.claim: The Prophet says every child of Adam erred or intended sin except Yahya, who did neither.
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ما من أحد من ولد آدم إلا وقد أخطأ

DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says everyone comes to Judgment with a sin except Yahya son of Zakariya.
DURR-FULL:v5p487#2/r8.anchor: عن عمرو بن العاص قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: كل بني آدم يأتي يوم القيامة وله ذنب

QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r9.claim: His peace at birth, death, and resurrection means protection from deviation and doctrinal error in life and from trial in the afterlife.
QUSHAYRI:v2p237/r9.anchor: يصونه عن الزيغ والعوج في العقيدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r1.claim: The greeting is attached to God's giving Yahya wisdom and addressed to Muslims, so they recognize his honor; it is God's praise and protection across his three life transitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r1.anchor: الأظهر أنه عطف على { وءاتيناه الحكم صبيا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r2.claim: سلام is a greeting containing praise or a prayer for safety; here it is God's greeting and praise, comparable to the greeting from a merciful Lord and the later greeting of Jesus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r2.anchor: فالمراد هنا سلام من الله عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r3.claim: Birth, death, and resurrection represent the beginning of worldly life, departure, and entry into the next life; اليوم means the time of each event, and the present tense vividly evokes Yahya's death, whose killing the Quran only summarizes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p77/r3.anchor: وهذه الأحوال الثلاثة المذكورة هنا أحوال ابتداء أطوار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r5.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r5.claim: Al-Tabari and others take salam as safety or protection.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r6.claim: Salam most likely means the familiar greeting, nobler than mere safety inferred from Yahya’s innocence; God greets him in moments of human weakness and need.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r6.anchor: الأظهر عندي أنها التحية المتعارفة فهي أشرف وأنبه من الأمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r7.claim: Al-Hasan transmits a meeting of Jesus and Yahya: Yahya asks Jesus to pray, but Jesus says Yahya should pray because God greeted Yahya while Jesus greeted himself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r7.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن الحسن أن عيسى ويحيى التقيا وهما ابنا الخالة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya’s father says some scholars infer Jesus’s superiority because the Qurʾanic account of Jesus greeting himself implies higher rank than a greeting from another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8/r8.anchor: انتزع بعض العلماء من هذه الآية في التسليم فضل عيسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r1.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r1.claim: One view takes salām as God's greeting to Yaḥya; this is Abū Sulayman's preferred view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه السلام المعروف من الله تعالى قال عطاء سلام عليه مني

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r2.claim: Another view understands salām as safety.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه بمعنى السلامة قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r3.claim: Day here means a time or occasion, so it can cover births and deaths that happen at night; compare 5:3.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r3.anchor: المراد باليوم الحين والوقت على ما بينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r4.claim: He says God's salām was upon Yaḥya when he was born.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسلام عليه حين ولد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r5.claim: In a meeting between Jesus and Yaḥya, Yaḥya says Jesus is better, but Jesus replies that Yaḥya is better because God greeted him while Jesus greeted himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r5.anchor: التقى يحيى وعيسى فقال يحيى لعيسى انت خير مني فقال عيسى ليحيى بل أنت خير مني

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r6.claim: His parallel report says God praised Yaḥya, while Jesus praised himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r6.anchor: إلا أنه قال اثنى الله عليك وأنا أثنيت على نفسي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r7.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r7.claim: Birth, death, and resurrection are a person's most lonely moments; God honored and protected Yaḥya in all three.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p215/r7.anchor: أوحش ما يكون الإنسان في ثلاثة مواطن يوم يولد فيرى نفسه خارجا

SULAMI:v1p423#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p423#3/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p423#3/r1.claim: God's greeting gives Yahya protection from every danger and preserves him from disobedience through death; Jesus's greeting also expresses praise of himself, made sweet in knowledge and subtle in kindness.
SULAMI:v1p423#3/r1.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله الهروي يقول : سمعت أبا بكر بن طاهر يقول : في قوله : وسلام عليه ) ^ تحية ربه له وأمان له من كل محذور

SULAMI:v1p423#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p423#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p423#3/r2.claim: Peace at the two ends of Yahya's life, birth and death, means he is kept from disobedience throughout.
SULAMI:v1p423#3/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : سلام في طرفي حيوته وموته من جريان مخالفة عليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r4.claim: Peace at birth, death, and resurrection means Yahya is secure in these three states.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r4.anchor: أي: له الأمان في هذه الثلاثة الأحوال.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r5.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r5.claim: Sufyan says people are loneliest at birth, death, and resurrection; God specially honored Yahya with peace at all three.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p217/r5.anchor: أوحش ما يكون الخلق في ثلاثة مواطن: يوم يولد، فيرى نفسه خارجا مما كان فيه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p218/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p218/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p218/r2.claim: Hasan reports that Jesus and Yahya each asked the other to seek forgiveness, each calling the other better; Jesus cites Yahya's divine peace as evidence of merit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p218/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: أن حسن قال: إن يحيى وعيسى، عليهما السلام، التقيا، فقال له عيسى: استغفر لي، أنت خير مني،

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r8.claim: Salām may mean safety from sin in worldly life and punishment in the next, God's peace, angelic greetings, or a command for the community to greet Yahya.
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r8.anchor: قيل: سلامة له في الدنيا من المعاصي وفي الآخرة من العذاب، وقيل: سلام الله عليه، وقيل: تسلم عليه الملائكة

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r9.claim: Peace at birth is a gift while peace at death and resurrection is reward; other readings describe protection from Satan, worldly trials, grave and Judgment terrors, or being raised among martyrs.
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r9.anchor: قيل: السلام يوم الولادة تفضل، وعند الموت والبعث ثواب، وقيل: سلامه له يوم ولد من صوت الشيطان ولطمه

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r10.claim: The word ḥayyan emphasizes the statement that Yahya will be raised.
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r10.anchor: وإنما قال: حيا تأكيدا لقوله: يوم يبعث

JISHUMI:v6p4530/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r16.claim: God's salām indicates Yahya's virtue and that his blessed state continued from birth until death.
JISHUMI:v6p4530/r16.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وسلام عليه) على فضل يحيى وأنه استمر أمره من لدن ولد إلى أن مات

JISHUMI:v6p4532/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r1.claim: Salām does not prove Yahya was better than Jesus: God's greeting and a commanded greeting are not distinguishable as proof of rank, and a report that they each declared the other better is unsound unless treated as mistaken self-estimation.
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r1.anchor: لأن السلام لا فرق بين أن يقول الله تعالى السلام عليك وبين أن يأمر نبيه بأن يقول ذلك

JISHUMI:v6p4532/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r2.claim: The claim that Satan struck Yahya at birth is false because Satan can only whisper, as scripture says.
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r2.anchor: لطم الشيطان غير صحيح؛ لأن الشيطان لا يقدر على غير الوسوسة

JISHUMI:v6p4532/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r3.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r3.claim: Al-Asamm says Jesus was a messenger to Yahya, citing the description of him as confirming a word from God; both lived at the same time and Yahya was three years older.
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r3.anchor: قال الأصم: كان عيسى رسولا إلى يحيى كما قال تعالى

JISHUMI:v6p4532/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r4.claim: The confirmation of Yahya's prophethood does not make Jesus a messenger specifically to him, just as Muhammad's confirmation of earlier prophets did not make them prophets to us; both were prophets, and God knows their relation.
JISHUMI:v6p4532/r4.anchor: لأن تصديقه بنبوته لا يوجب كونه نبيا إليه، كما أن نبينا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#2/r1.claim: God grants Yahya peace in the three vulnerable states named in the verse: birth, death, and resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#2/r1.anchor: سلم الله عليه في هذه الأحوال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#2/r2.speaker: ابن عيينة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUyaynah calls these the loneliest and most frightening circumstances.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عيينة : إنها أوحش المواطن

MUQATIL:19:13-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:13-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:13-15/r3.claim: God's peace on Yahya at birth, death, and resurrection refers to those times; yawm can mean 'when,' as in the creation and resurrection passages cited here.
MUQATIL:19:13-15/r3.anchor: يعني على يحيى، عليه السلام، { يوم ولد } ، يعني حين ولد، مثل قوله سبحانه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#7/r1.claim: God's peace is safety for Yahya: from Satan at birth, the grave's trials at death, and the greatest terror at resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#7/r1.anchor: ﴿ وسلام عليه ﴾ آمان من الله له ﴿ يوم ولد ﴾ من أن يناله الشيطان ﴿ ويوم يموت ﴾ من فتاني القبر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#7/r2.speaker: ابن عيينة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#7/r2.claim: Ibn Uyayna says the resurrection is the most desolate of the three stations.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p32#7/r2.anchor: قال ابن عيينة إنها أوحش المواطن

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r6.speaker: الطبري وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r6.claim: Al-Tabari and others interpret peace upon Yahya as safety.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers a greeting from God over mere safety, since safety is a lesser baseline and God’s greeting honors Yahya at life’s vulnerable transitions; Qurtubi calls this a good view.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r7.anchor: والأظهر عندي أنها التحية المتعارفة فهي أشرف وأنبه من الأمان

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r8.claim: Al-Tabari transmits Hasan’s report that Jesus and Yahya, maternal cousins, debated which was better; Jesus said Yahya was honored by God’s greeting, whereas Jesus had greeted himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r8.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن الحسن أن عيسى ويحيى التقيا وهما ابنا الخالة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r9.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r9.claim: Some scholars infer Jesus’s greater rank because he confidently pronounced peace upon himself, while Yahya was greeted by God; Ibn Atiyya says each view has its case.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:13-15/r9.anchor: فانتزع بعض العلماء من هذه الآية في التسليم فضل عيسى

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r1.claim: The continuation of al-Ṭabarī's first view says God's peace protects Yaḥyā from grave punishment at death and punishment at resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r1.anchor: ويوم يموت } أي وأمان عليه من عذاب القبر : { ويوم يبعث حيا

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r2.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r2.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says birth, death, and resurrection are the most isolating moments for people; God honored Yaḥyā with peace at all three.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r2.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة أوحش ما يكون الخلق في ثلاثة مواطن يوم يولد

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن نفطوية
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Naftawayh reads birth as the first sight of this world, death as the first sight of the afterlife, and resurrection as the first sight of Paradise and Hell; calling him alive points to martyrdom.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r3.anchor: وسلام عليه يوم ولد } أي أول ما يرى الدنيا { ويوم يموت

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r4.claim: The greeting may come from God or the angels, and its honor is the same because angels greet only by God's command.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r4.anchor: يمكن أن يكون من الله تعالى وأن يكون من الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r5.claim: Yaḥyā has a special distinction over other prophets because his greeting explicitly includes the day he was born, unlike the salutations to Noah and Abraham.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r5.anchor: ليحيى مزية في هذا السلام على ما لسائر الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r6.claim: A report says Jesus told Yaḥyā he was better because God greeted Yaḥyā while Jesus greeted himself.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r6.anchor: الثالث : روي أن عيسى عليه السلام قال ليحيى عليه السلام : أنت أفضل مني

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī says this comparison is unpersuasive: Jesus was infallible and spoke only by God's command, so his greeting himself is like God's greeting Yaḥyā.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r7.anchor: وهذا ليس يقوى لأن سلام عيسى على نفسه يجري مجرى سلام الله على يحيى

RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r8.claim: Peace at birth must be a divine gift because Yaḥyā had done nothing to earn it; peace at death and resurrection could instead be reward.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165/r8.anchor: السلام عليه يوم ولد لا بد وأن يكون تفضلا من الله تعالى

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r55.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r55.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r55.claim: Peace at John’s birth means protection from Satan; at death, exemption from grave trials.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r55.anchor: protection for him against the evil promptings of Satan (R, Ṭ); the blessing upon him the day he dies indicates that he is exempt from the trials of the grave

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r56.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r56.speaker: Ṭ, R
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r56.claim: Peace when John is raised means he will avoid resurrection dread or punishment.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r56.anchor: he will not suffer the fear and dread that will overcome others on the Day of Resurrection (Ṭ) or experience any punishment (R, Ṭ).

NAHHAS:v3p9/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p9/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p9/r2.claim: سلام is nominative as subject; an indefinite subject suits the prayer, and سلام عليك equals سلام الله عليك in Arabic.
NAHHAS:v3p9/r2.anchor: رفع بالابتداء وحسن الابتداء بالنكرة لأن فيها معنى الدعاء

TAB-FULL:v15p481/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p481/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p481/r1.claim: Yaḥyā was dutiful, quick to obey and love his parents, never disobedient to them.
TAB-FULL:v15p481/r1.anchor: والديه، ولكنه كان لله ولوالديه متواضعا متذللا، يأتمر لما أمر به

TAB-FULL:v15p481/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p481/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p481/r2.claim: He was humble and submissive, obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions, never disobeying God or his parents.
TAB-FULL:v15p481/r2.anchor: والديه، ولكنه كان لله ولوالديه متواضعا متذللا، يأتمر لما أمر به، وينتهي عما نهي عنه

TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r1.claim: God's peace protects Yaḥyā at birth from Satan's harm to which other human children are exposed.
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r1.anchor: روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «كل بني آدم يأتي يوم القيامة وله ذنب

TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r2.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r2.claim: A report says every child of Adam reaches Judgment Day with a sin except Yaḥyā son of Zakariyyā.
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r2.anchor: «كل بني آدم يأتي يوم القيامة وله ذنب إلا ما كان من يحيى بن زكريا»

TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r4.claim: Peace at death protects Yaḥyā from the grave's examiners and its terrors; at resurrection it protects him from punishment and the Great Terror.
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r4.anchor: وأمان له من عذاب الله يوم القيامة، يوم الفزع الأكبر، من أن يروعه شيء

TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r5.claim: He says birth, death, and resurrection are the most lonely moments, and God singled Yaḥyā out with peace at all three.
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r5.anchor: أوحش ما يكون الخلق في ثلاثة مواطن: يوم يولد فيرى نفسه خارجا مما كان فيه

TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r6.claim: A report says Jesus and Yaḥyā each asked the other for forgiveness; Jesus said Yaḥyā was better because God had saluted him.
TAB-FULL:v15p481#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، أن الحسن، قال: إن عيسى ويحيى التقيا فقال له عيسى

TABATABAI:19:7-9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r4.claim: Yahya receives unique descriptions: wisdom as a child, leadership and chastity, and peace at birth, death, and resurrection; Jesus shared them but was born later, though they were cousins.
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r4.anchor: نعته في كلامه بنعوت لم ينعت به أحدا من أنبيائه وأوليائه قبله

TABATABAI:19:13-15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r6.claim: Salam means a state in which what one encounters is fitting and unfeared, unlike amn, which only means absence of feared harm; its indefinite form conveys grandeur.
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r6.anchor: وتنكير السلام لإفادة التفخيم أي سلام فخيم عليه مما يكرهه في هذه الأيام الثلاثة

TABATABAI:19:13-15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r7.claim: The three days open distinct worlds: birth brings earthly safety, death brings bliss in the intermediate realm, and resurrection brings true life without fatigue.
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r7.anchor: فسلام عليه يوم ولد فلا يمسه مكروه في الدنيا يزاحم سعادته

TABATABAI:19:13-15/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:19:13-15/r8.claim: Some say the added word alive signals that Yahya will be killed as a martyr.

TABATABAI:19:1-15#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#2/r1.claim: The wording change for birth, death, and resurrection portrays the greeting of peace as applying during Jesus's lifetime.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#2/r1.anchor: لتمثيل أن التسليم في حال حياته عليه السلام

TABATABAI:19:15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:15/r1.claim: Reports through Sunni routes give varying forms of John's sinlessness; the author restricts their broad wording to infallible prophets and Imams, attributing its apparent excess to narrators' paraphrase.
TABATABAI:19:15/r1.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي من طرق أهل السنة بألفاظ مختلفة

TABATABAI:19:15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:15/r2.claim: Reports describe John's asceticism: he ate grass, wore palm fiber, and wept from fear of God until tears made a track on his face.
TABATABAI:19:15/r2.anchor: يأكل العشب ويلبس الليف وبكى من خشية الله حتى اتخذت الدموع مجرى في وجهه

TABATABAI:19:15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r3.speaker: قرة
TABATABAI:19:15/r3.claim: Qurra says the sky wept only for John and Husayn; another report from al-Sadiq adds that both killers were illegitimate sons.
TABATABAI:19:15/r3.anchor: عن قرة قال ما بكت السماء على أحد إلا على يحيى بن زكريا

TABATABAI:19:15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:19:15/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says God told Muhammad that seventy thousand were killed on account of John and 140,000 through the Prophet's grandson.
TABATABAI:19:15/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال أوحى الله إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:19:15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r6.speaker: علي موسى الرضا
TABATABAI:19:15/r6.claim: Al-Riḍa says the most frightening moments are birth, death, and resurrection; God granted John peace at all three, as Jesus also proclaimed peace over himself at those stages.
TABATABAI:19:15/r6.anchor: قال سمعت أبا الحسن الرضا عليه السلام يقول إن أوحش ما يكون هذا الخلق

TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.claim: The Qur'an praises John as affirming Jesus's prophethood, a leader, chaste, prophet, righteous, elect and guided; God named him uniquely, gave him wisdom as a child, and greeted him at the three stages.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.anchor: كان مصدقا بكلمة من الله وهو تصديقه بنبوة المسيح

TABRISI:19:13-15/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r9.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:19:13-15/r9.claim: The greeting of peace on the three days is from God.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r9.anchor: أي سلام عليه منا في هذه الأيام عن عطاء

TABRISI:19:13-15/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:13-15/r10.claim: Hayyan emphasizes that Yahya will truly be raised alive.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r10.anchor: وإنما قال حيا تأكيدا لقوله: { يبعث }

TABRISI:19:13-15/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:19:13-15/r11.claim: Another view says Yahya is raised with the martyrs because they are described as alive.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r11.anchor: وقيل: يعني أنه يبعث مع الشهداء لأنهم وصفوا بأنهم أحياء

TABRISI:19:13-15/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:13-15/r12.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
TABRISI:19:13-15/r12.claim: Sufyan says the three most lonely moments are birth, death, and resurrection.
TABRISI:19:13-15/r12.anchor: أوحش ما يكون الإنسان في ثلاثة مواطن يوم ولد

THALABI:v6p207#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r15.speaker: الحلبي
THALABI:v6p207#2/r15.claim: Al-Halabi says the peace is from God for Yahya at birth, death, and resurrection.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r15.anchor: وسلام عليه قال الحلبي: سلام له منا حين ولد وحين يموت وحين يبعث حيا.

THALABI:v6p207#2/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207#2/r16.speaker: الحسن عن قتادة
THALABI:v6p207#2/r16.claim: Hasan reports that Jesus and Yahya each asked the other to seek forgiveness, each calling the other better; Jesus said he had blessed himself while God blessed Yahya.
THALABI:v6p207#2/r16.anchor: عن قتادة عن الحسن أن يحيى وعيسى عليهما السلام التقيا فقال له عيسى: استغفر لي فأنت خير مني،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r1.claim: An indefinite سلام can begin a sentence because the noun is commonly used this way; common nouns may begin a sentence when their indefinite sense nearly equals the definite.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r1.anchor: أبو إسحاق: (سلام مما يبتدأ به في النكره؛ لأنه اسم يكثر استعماله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r2.claim: God's peace is with Yahya in these periods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r2.anchor: يريد سلام عليه مني في هذه الأيام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r3.claim: The greeting means safety for Yahya from God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r3.anchor: الكلبي: (سلامة له منا) (¬3). وقال سفيان بن عيينه:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r4.claim: Birth, death, and resurrection are the three most unsettling times; God singled Yahya out with honor by greeting him at all three.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r4.anchor: سفيان بن عيينه: (أوحش ما يكون الخلق في ثلاثة مواطن: يوم ولد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r5.claim: The days denote periods including nights, since a person may be born or die at night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r5.anchor: ابن الأنباري: (لم يقصد باليوم قصد يوم واحد؛ لأنه يجوز أن يموت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r6.claim: The verse means that peace is upon Yahya during the period of his birth and the following periods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r6.anchor: وتلخيص معنى الآية: ويسلم عليه في زمان مولده، وكذلك ما بعده.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r7.claim: God greeted Yahya at the moment he was born.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p210#2/r7.anchor: الكلبي عن ابن عباس: (وسلم عليه حين ولد)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:11-16/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:11-16/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:11-16/r5.claim: God's peace on Yahya means He preserved him in the life stages named.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:11-16/r5.anchor: وسلام عليه } سلامة له منا في الأحوال التي ذكرها، يريد أن الله سبحانه سلمه في هذه الأحوال.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r3.claim: Al-Suddī glosses peace at Yahya's birth and death as those times, and peace at his rising as the Day of Resurrection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r3.anchor:
{وسلام عليه يوم ولد} [مريم: 15] يعني: حين ولد.
{ويوم يموت} [مريم: 15] يعني: وحين يموت.
{ويوم يبعث حيا} [مريم: 15] يوم القيامة.
وهو تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that Jesus and Yahya each asked the other to seek forgiveness, with Jesus finally insisting Yahya was better; Jesus said he had declared peace upon himself while God declared peace upon Yahya, and al-Ḥasan says Jesus recognized the honor of that distinction.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r4.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، عن الحسن أن يحيى وعيسى التقيا، فقال له عيسى: استغفر لي أنت خير مني.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r5.claim: Yaḥyā links Yahya's greeting to 19:15 and Jesus's greeting to 19:30–31 and 19:33.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r5.anchor: قال يحيى: يعني قول الله تبارك وتعالى في يحيى: {وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا} [مريم: 15] وقال عيسى:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r6.claim: The linked words of Jesus include his statement that he is God's servant and prophet, blessed wherever he is, and the greeting of peace at birth, death, and resurrection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218/r6.anchor: {قال إني عبد الله آتاني الكتاب وجعلني نبيا {30} وجعلني مباركا أين ما كنت} [مريم: 30-31] إلى قوله: {والسلام علي يوم ولدت ويوم أموت ويوم أبعث حيا} [مريم: 33]

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:15/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:15/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:15/r1.claim: Yahya's seven virtues are wisdom, compassion, purity, piety, respect for parents, freedom from tyranny, and obedience; God's care accompanies him at birth, death, and resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:15/r1.anchor: bütün bu hallerde yani dünyaya gelirken, dünyadan giderken ve kıyamet gününde kabirden kalkarken Allah’ın inâyetinin onunla beraber olacağı bildirilmiştir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prophets in Adam’s, Noah’s, and Abraham’s lines preached monotheism, prayer, and zakāh, but their followers turned to polytheism, abandoned the rites, and followed innovations and desires.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: all celebrated prophets born in the progeny of Adam (sws), Noah (sws) and Abraham (sws) preached monotheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet is urged to persevere against their hostility and is given glad tidings of success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is urged to show perseverance on their attitude and given glad tidings of success.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The adversaries mistake worldly success for proof of their truth; it is only respite until the truth is conclusively conveyed and they have no excuse when seized.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they regard their worldly successes in contrast to the believers to be a reason of their own veracity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Jesus and Mary are prominent because Christians and Jews secretly supported Quraysh; the Qur’an exposes the People of the Book to show they cannot support a truthless cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Christians too had begun to secretly support the Quraysh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Zacharias story introduces Mary’s story and counters Christians who treat Jesus’s miraculous birth as proof of his divinity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This incident forms a prelude to the anecdote of Mary (sws) mentioned subsequently.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Angels greeted John with peace and blessings at birth, death, and resurrection, giving him God's favor through every phase despite how people treated him in this world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: welcomed him in every phase of life: the day he was born, the day he died

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the ordinary greeting; the honor is that God greets Yahya at the moments of greatest human weakness and need.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r5.anchor: والأظهر أنها التحية المتعارفة وإنما الشرف في أن سلم الله عليه وحياه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r6.claim: A report from al-Ḥasan says Jesus and his cousin Yahya met; Yahya asked Jesus to pray for him, but Jesus said Yahya was better because God had greeted him while Jesus greeted himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r6.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن الحسن أن عيسى ويحيى عليهما السلام التقيا وهما ابنا الخالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī explains the greeting at birth as protection from Satan, at death as protection from the grave's punishment, and at resurrection as protection from God's punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r7.anchor: يوم ولد أي أمان عليه من أن يتاله الشيطان ويوم يموت أي أمان من عذاب القبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī sees 'raised alive' as hinting that Yahya was among the martyrs, who live with their Lord.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r8.anchor: وفي قوله ويوم يبعث حيا تنبيه على كونه من الشهداء لقوله بل أحياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī allows the greeting to come from God or the angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r9.anchor: وهذا السلام يحتمل أن يكون من الله وأن يكون من الملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r10.claim: The author prefers God as the source, since the context says that God gave Yahya wisdom.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p246/r10.anchor: والأظهر أنه من الله لأنه في سياق وآتيناه الحكم

BURHAN:v4p92/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p92/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p92/r1.claim: In Jesus' greeting, the definite al-salam evokes the prayer's source in God's name al-Salam; invoking a divine name exposes the speaker to what that name denotes.
BURHAN:v4p92/r1.anchor: والسلام اسم من اسمائه مشتق من السلامه

DAMGHANI:v1p506/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p506/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p506/r8.claim: Yawm can mean a time or occasion, as in the times of birth, death, resurrection, travel, residence, and harvest.
DAMGHANI:v1p506/r8.anchor: وسلام عليه يوم ولد ويوم يموت ويوم يبعث حيا يعني حين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r1.claim: The indefinite سلام signals broad, comprehensive peace, while definite السلام is specific or restricted.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r1.anchor: والنكرة عادة تدل على الشمول والعموم والمعرفة تدل على الإختصاص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r3.claim: Yahya's greeting is indefinite because it comes from God, while Isa uses the definite form when speaking of himself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p645/r3.anchor: وتحية سيدنا يحيى - عليه السلام - هي من الله تعالى لذا جاءت بالتنكير (سلام عليه) أما تحية عيسى - عليه السلام - فهي من نفسه فجاءت بالمعرفة
